bounds.bound_starts: After the initial asyncio.wait_for reports TimeoutError; cancellation delivery before that handler and event-loop scheduling are outside the two-step allowance.
bounds.cleanup_behavior: Kill the direct clone process; bound post-kill communicate; close the asyncio subprocess transport to release owned pipes; if draining did not complete, make one bounded process wait; raise ExtractionError so extraction finally cleanup removes partial materialization.

preserved_contracts: At most two clone attempts for slashed refs, exercised by existing scoped tests.
Source caps, selected-source safety and normal temp-workspace cleanup, exercised by existing scoped tests.
No production limit, dependency, configuration, shared contract, benchmark input or retained historical evidence changed.
limitations: Process reaping is best effort if the OS or event loop fails to report exit within the bounded wait; no race-proof or cancellation-safe guarantee is claimed.
Only the direct clone process is killed. No process-group or descendant kill is attempted; closing Fugu's transport releases Fugu-owned pipe handles but does not guarantee helper processes terminate.
Timeout cleanup uses asyncio.Process._transport because Process has no public close method; SubprocessTransport.close is documented for Python 3.10 and closes owned pipes.
